opex.text: Our principal demands for funds are for: (i) acquisition of real estate and real estate-related investments, (ii) payment of acquisition-related expenses and operating expenses, (iii) payment of dividends/distributions, (iv) payment of principal and interest on current and any future outstanding indebtedness, (v) redemptions of our securities under our redemption plans, and (vi) capital improvements, development projects, and property-related expenditures.

costs.text: Our principal demands for funds are for: (i) acquisition of real estate and real estate-related investments, (ii) payment of acquisition-related expenses and operating expenses, (iii) payment of dividends/distributions, (iv) payment of principal and interest on current and any future outstanding indebtedness, (v) redemptions of our securities under our redemption plans, and (vi) capital improvements, development projects, and property-related expenditures.

nonop.text: Interest expense of $7,431 during the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased $1,060 or 16.6% in comparison to the same period in 2025. The increase in interest expense was primarily driven by elevated interest rates and increased mortgage balance for the three months ended June 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. Interest expense as a percentage of total revenues for the three months ending June 30, 2026 and 2025 was 16.1% and 14.8%, respectively.

net.text: Funds From Operations (FFO) applicable to common shares and limited partnership units means net income (computed in accordance with GAAP), excluding gains (or losses) from sales of property, plus depreciation and amortization, and after adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures. Adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures will be calculated to reflect funds from operations on the same basis.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $27,756 and $20,664 for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, which consists primarily of net income from property operations adjusted for non-cash depreciation and amortization.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense of $7,399 during the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased $703 or 10.5% in comparison to the same period in 2025. Amortization expense will continue to decrease as lease intangibles become fully amortized but will increase upon acquisitions of intangible assets. Depreciation and amortization expense as a percentage of total revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 was 16.0% and 15.6%, respectively.

Residential.text: Residential revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased $2,991 or 6.1% in comparison to the same period for 2025. Residential properties acquired since June 30, 2025 contributed approximately $540 of the increase in total residential revenues in the three months ended June 30, 2026. The remaining increase is due to increased rent charges at our stabilized properties. Residential revenues comprised 89.2% of total revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to 88.7% of total revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2025.

Commercial.text: For the three months ended June 30, 2026 total commercial revenues increased $120 or 2.5% in comparison to the same period for 2025. The increase is primarily attributed to increased rent charges at our stabilized properties during the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025. Commercial revenues comprised 10.8% of the total revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to 11.3% of total revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2025. As commercial properties are sold, commercial revenues are expected to continue declining as a percentage of total revenues.

nonop.text: Interest expense of $7,370 during the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $542 or 7.9% in comparison to the same period in 2025. The increase in interest expense was primarily driven by elevated interest rates and increased mortgage balance for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was partially offset by a $245 decrease in interest on our lines of credit. Interest expense as a percentage of total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was 15.9% and 15.6%, respectively.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $51,238 and $37,828 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, which consists primarily of net income from property operations adjusted for non-cash depreciation and amortization.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense of $7,093 during the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased $ (499) or (6.6)% in comparison to the same period in 2025. The decrease is primarily due to a $722 decrease in amortization expense as lease intangibles became fully amortized, partially offset by a $273 increase in depreciation expense. Amortization expense will continue to decrease as lease intangibles become fully amortized but will increase upon acquisitions of intangible assets. Depreciation and amortization expense as a percentage of total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was 15.3% and 17.4%, respectively.

Residential.text: Residential revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $2,888 or 7.5% in comparison to the same period for 2025. Residential properties acquired since September 30, 2025 contributed approximately $540 of the increase in total residential revenues in the three months ended September 30, 2026. The remaining increase is due to increased rent charges at our stabilized properties. Residential revenues comprised 89.8% of total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 88.6% of total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Commercial.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026 total commercial revenues decreased $ (248) or 5.0% in comparison to the same period for 2025. The decrease is primarily attributed to lower commercial occupancy (85.7% at September 30, 2026, compared to 90.0% at September 30, 2025), lower common area maintenance reimbursements and the sale of Parkway Office Building in August 2026. Commercial revenues comprised 10.2% of the total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 11.4% of total revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2025. As commercial properties are sold, commercial revenues are expected to continue declining as a percentage of total revenues.
